A. R. Coo!

Mr Robert Brzozowsky is an
Austrian Jew and is said to have
obtained his medical diploma at Prague.
He has been residing in Shanghai from
time to time during the past three years
during which period he travelled once
to Europe, 1926/7, via Siberia when he
was absent about 10 months. On two
occasions he travelled to Mukden.
It is alleged that he has connections
with the Bolsheviki and each time
he returns to Shanghai is always flush
with money. He opened a hospital at
98 Rue Massenet with funds alleged to
have been received from the Bolsheviki.
He ran into debt, fell into financial
difficulties, sold by the Hospital together
with some other private property which did
not belong to him and for which the
French Police authorities issued a summons
against him.

After returning from Europe he opened
a medical cabinet at No 20 Museum Road
and a watch maintained over these
premises for a month disclosed that
no patients or sick persons ever visited him.
Mr Brzozowsky writes Russian and
states that he was a doctor in Russia

(C.I.D.) Office Notes
01. V.C.O.I.

The records of the passenger list in
the local office of the German Norddeutscher
Lloyd steamship Co. show that an Austrian
named Rudolph Rolf Henkel boarded
their steamer, the s.s. "Coblenz," at Colombo,
India on November 11th 1928 for Shanghai.
According to arrangements when booking his ticket
the local office of the above Company was to make
the necessary connections to enable Henkel to
proceed to Japan, but he failed to make
reservations, although he gave the passenger
department here to understand on his arrival
that he intended to proceed to that country.
He received no letter from Osaka containing
money addressed to him care of the office
of the above mentioned shipping company.
The clerk at the passenger department
asserts that the individual shown in the
attached photograph is not Henkel.

Henkel took up his residence at
1976 Route des Soeurs, and Germans who are
personally acquainted with him state
that he receives a remittance of monthly
money from home through the Austrian
Consul - Mr. F. Winkler.

Henkel entered the employ of the
Austrian firm "Moebius" (W. O. Moebius)
6 Kiangse Road, which supplies steel
for Chinese arsenals etc. On January 12th 1929
he removed to Room 403, Foreign Y.M.C.A.,
Bubbling Well Road to which institution he
was recommended by an Italian named
Tomasi. Mr. Duff, secretary of the Foreign Y.M.C.A.
states that Henkel is not the same person as
that shown in the photograph.

(刑事侦缉处) 办公笔记
01. V.C.O.I.

德国北德意志劳埃德轮船公司（Norddeutscher Lloyd）本地办事处的乘客名单记录显示，一名名叫鲁道夫·罗尔夫·亨克尔（Rudolph Rolf Henkel）的奥地利人于1928年11月11日在印度科伦坡登上了该公司的“科布伦茨”号（s.s. "Coblenz"）轮船前往上海。根据订票时的安排，上述公司的本地办事处本应进行必要的联络，以便亨克尔前往日本，但他并未进行预订，尽管他在抵达时让这里的客运部门以为他打算前往该国。他没有收到从大阪寄来、通过上述航运公司办事处转交给他并内含钱款的信件。
客运部门的职员声称，附件照片中的人并非亨克尔。

亨克尔居住在姐妹路1976号，与他私交的德国人称，他通过奥地利领事——F. 温克勒先生（Mr. F. Winkler）——从国内收到每月汇款。

亨克尔受雇于江西路6号的奥地利商行“莫比乌斯”（Moebius）（W. O. Moebius），该商行向中国兵工厂等供应钢材。1929年1月12日，他搬至静安寺路外国青年会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.）403室，他是经一名叫托马西（Tomasi）的意大利人推荐入住该机构的。外国青年会秘书达夫先生（Mr. Duff）表示，亨克尔与照片中的人不是同一人。

page_data.en:
On February 20th Henkl applied to Messrs Bickhoff
& Co. in Kiangse Road in reply to an advertisement
for a position, which however he was unable
to fulfill owing to his lack of knowledge of
the English language for commercial purposes.
Simultaneously, enquiries made by Mr.
Reuss of Bickhoff & Co. at "Moskino" showed
that Henkl was terminating his services with
the latter firm for the same reason.
He informed Mr Reuss that he had come
to Shanghai direct from India where he
had held a position for one year after which
he had the option to return home or come out
East. He added that his father was an
Austrian naval officer and gave the following
persons as references: - F. Winkel, Austrian
Consul and K. Ellacek, Weissner & Co.,
60 Kiangse Road. Mr. Reuss, on being shown
the photograph thought there was a resemblance
but finally failed to recognize Henkl as the
same individual as shown in the photograph.
Herr Gustav von Kreitner stated that
Mr. F. Winkel the Austrian Consul approached
him with the request to help find a job for
Henkl. Attached herewith is Henkl's
letter addressed to Von Kreitner confirming
Von Kreitner's statement. This gentleman
saw Henkl on two occasions only and he
informed me that he does not trust Henkl's
books. Furthermore, he stated that Henkl told
him his father was an admiral but in his
curriculum vitae he refers to his father a high officer
of the Austrian navy. Henkl also said he had
been an aviator during the war, but in his curriculum
vitae he styles himself as observation officer. Von
Kreitner said that the photograph was such a
poor one he was unable to recognize Henkl.
Henkl at present is giving lessons in German
language to Judge Liding of the Provisional Court.

HR. 3
729
March 5, 1929.
John F. Cook
page_data.zh:
2月20日，亨克尔回复江西路比克霍夫公司（Messrs Bickhoff & Co.）的一则招聘广告申请职位，但由于缺乏商业英语知识而未能胜任。与此同时，比克霍夫公司的鲁伊斯先生（Mr. Reuss）向“莫斯科诺”（Moskino）查询得知，亨克尔正因同样原因终止在该公司的服务。他告诉鲁伊斯先生，他直接从印度来到上海，在那里任职一年后，他可以选择回国或来到东方。他补充说，他的父亲是奥地利海军军官，并提供以下人员作为推荐人：F. 温克尔（F. Winkel），奥地利领事；K. 埃拉切克（K. Ellacek），魏斯纳公司（Weissner & Co.），江西路60号。鲁伊斯先生在看过照片后认为有些相似，但最终未能认出亨克尔就是照片中的那个人。
古斯塔夫·冯·克雷特纳先生表示，奥地利领事 F. 温克尔先生曾找他，请求帮助为亨克尔找工作。随函附上亨克尔致冯·克雷特纳的信件，证实了冯·克雷特纳的说法。这位绅士仅见过亨克尔两次，他告诉我，他不信任亨克尔的账目。此外，他表示亨克尔告诉他父亲是海军上将，但在其简历中却称父亲为奥地利海军的高级军官。亨克尔还说他曾在战争期间担任飞行员，但在简历中自称为观察员军官。冯·克雷特纳说照片质量太差，他无法认出亨克尔。亨克尔目前正给临时法院的李丁法官（Judge Liding）上德语课。

Curriculum Vitae.

I was born in Vienna, Austria, on 14-12-1897
as the son of a high officer in the Austrian Navy. My
ancestors for the last three generations held high positions
in the Navy. After graduation from the Gymnasiums (in Vienna
and in Switzerland) I studied philosophy (Orientalistic,
Sinologie) for 1 year and completed my high school education
in "Bauhaus" in Weimar. During the war I served as an officer
in the 3rd Uhlanen Regiment serving for several years at the
front and was engaged in the Italian and Rumanian offensives.
I was then transferred to the General Staff and obtained the
extensive task of organizing, in the Venetian Province, District
authorities and establishing the Field Police. As this territory
was not lying far from the front and was occupied by a large
number of troops and civilian population the task was one of
great responsibility. After being engaged for six months as a
District officer I was transferred to the Flying Corps and was
engaged in several enemy flights (photographic Service) and
air fights. I was wounded several times and obtained a
number of distinctions. During my activity as a District
officer I was in charge of a large bureau, attachment of Field
Police, spy service and an agricultural Department, etc. I was
specially praised by the Army field command. After the war I
was engaged in various occupations, among others, as a bank clerk,

个人简历。

我于1897年12月14日出生于奥地利维也纳，父亲是奥地利海军的高级军官。我的祖先在三代人中均在海军担任高职。从文理中学毕业后（在维也纳和瑞士），我学习了1年哲学（东方学、汉学），并在魏玛的“包豪斯”完成了高等教育。战争期间，我在第3乌兰骑兵团服役，在前线服役数年，参与了意大利和罗马尼亚的攻势。随后我被调往总参谋部，承担了在威尼斯省组织地区当局和建立战地警察的重大任务。由于该地区离前线不远，驻扎着大量军队和平民人口，这项任务责任重大。在担任地区军官六个月后，我被调往飞行队，参与了几次敌后飞行（摄影服务）和空战。我多次负伤，并获得多项嘉奖。在担任地区军官期间，我负责一个大型局处，附属战地警察、间谍服务和农业部门等。我受到陆军野战司令部的特别表彰。战后，我从事过各种职业，其中包括银行职员，

as editor in Rome and a journalist in Berlin and Paris. In
the last occupation I was in charge of several German
organs appearing in Paris (The Chroniques du Jour and
Pariser Kurier) the policy of which supported an

perfect knowledge of the important languages (German, French,
Italian and English) and hope with my abilities as an organizer

that I spent the greater part of last year in India to

CURRICULUM VITAE

Ich bin in Wien, Oesterreich, am 14.XII.1897 als Sohn eines Offiziers der oesterreichischen Kriegsmarine geboren. Meine Vorfahren bekleideten seit drei Generationen in der Marine hohe Posten.

Nach Absolvierung des Gymnasiums (in Wien und in der Schweiz) studierte ich ein Jahr Philosophie (Orientalistik, Sinologie) und vollendete meine Hochschulausbildung am "Bauhaus" in Weimar.

Im Kriege diente ich als Offizier i III.Ulmarregiment, leistete mehrere Jahre Frontdienst und machte die rumänische und italienische Offensive mit. Dann wurde ich zum Generalstab kommandiert und erhielt die umfangreiche organisatorische Aufgabe, in einer Provinz des besetzten Venetiens die Bezirksverwaltung und die Feldpolizei einzurichten. Da dieses Territorium nicht weit hinter der Front lag, und ebenso von grossen Truppenmassen wie von Zivilbevölkerung besetzt war, war meine Aufgabe ebenso schwierig wie verantwortungsvoll.

Nach sechsmonatiger Tätigkeit als Bezirksoffizier wurde ich zur Fliegertruppe versetzt und absolvierte eine Reihe von Feindflügen (Photodienst) und Luftkämpfen. Ich wurde mehrfach verwundet und erhielt eine Reihe von Auszeichnungen.

Für meine Tätigkeit als Bezirksoffizier, in welcher ich ein umfangreiches Büro, eine Abteilung der Feldpolizei und des Spionagedienstes, eine landwirtschaftliche Abteilung usw. leitete, wurde ich von Armeegruppenkommando besonders belobt.

Nach dem Kriege arbeitete ich in den verschiedensten Berufen, so z.B. als Bankbeamter, als Verlagsdirektor in Rom, als Journalist in Berlin und Paris.

In letzter Eigenschaft leitete ich mehrere in Paris deutsch erscheinende Organe (Les chroniques du jour, Pariser Kurier), deren politischer Teil die Annäherung Deutschlands und Frankreichs unterstützte.

Ich beherrsche perfekt die grossen Sprachen (Deutsch, französisch, italienisch,

个人简历

我于1897年12月14日出生于奥地利维也纳，父亲是奥地利海军军官。我的祖先三代以来在海军中担任高职。

在完成文理中学学业后（在维也纳和瑞士），我学习了一年哲学（东方学、汉学），并在魏玛的“包豪斯”完成了高等教育。

战争期间，我在第3乌兰骑兵团担任军官，在前线服役数年，参加了罗马尼亚和意大利的攻势。随后我被派往总参谋部，接受了在威尼斯被占领省份的一个地区建立地区行政机构和战地警察的广泛组织任务。由于该领土位于前线后方不远处，且既有大量部队又有平民居住，我的任务既困难又责任重大。

在担任地区军官六个月后，我被调往飞行部队，执行了一系列敌后飞行（摄影服务）和空战任务。我多次负伤，并获得了一系列勋章。

在我担任地区军官期间，我领导着一个庞大的办公室、战地警察和间谍服务部门、农业部门等，因此受到集团军司令部的特别表扬。

战后，我从事过各种不同的职业，例如银行职员、罗马的出版主管、柏林和巴黎的记者。

在后一职位上，我负责几家在巴黎出版的德文报刊（《每日纪事》、《巴黎信使》），其政治版面支持德法接近。

我完美掌握主要语言（德语、法语、意大利语、

H. B. M. Consulate-General,

19th. February, 1929.

My dear Aiers,

In continuation of our personal
correspondence on the subject of Rolf Henkl, I have
received information by telegram from India that
there is no record of any one of this name having
visited India. This makes the matter still more
suspicious as the passports of all Germans and
Austrians are carefully examined in India at ports
of entry and their movements are reported on in the
Weekly Police Abstracts of Intelligence. Would it
be possible for you to have a look at Henkl's pass-
port and ascertain whether it bears any endorsements
or examination marks by the Police and Passport
Authorities in India. Prima facie it would appear
that Henkl never visited India or that he travelled
in that country under a different name.

Yours sincerely,
C. M. Hallard
